latin: Ex eo nomine quo dei nominant amorem, patet diligenter aduertenti quod in actu amoris non est foelicitas.
translation: From the name by which the gods name love, it is clear to one who attends carefully that happiness does not consist in the act of love.
translation_note: 'foelicitas' is Farmer's transcription of 'felicitas' (happiness, beatitude); Busi and Ebgi's apparatus identifies the two sources behind 'the name by which the gods call love' (busi2014:6542).
translator: original translation, drafted 2026-09-26 by WRITER-full-batch15, from Latin at farmer1998:22994
attribution: Pico's own opinion, in the doctrine of Plato (section 5>, farmer1998:22132).

sources.pico_relation: identified in Busi and Ebgi's apparatus as a source for 'the name by which the gods call love'

sources.text: Pseudo-Dionysius the Areopagite, De divinis nominibus I (589a)
sources.pico_relation: identified in Busi and Ebgi's apparatus as a second source for the same motif

doctrine: The thesis holds that from the name by which the gods call love, it is clear to a careful observer that happiness does not consist in the act of love (farmer1998:22994). Farmer's note places it in the series he begins discussing at thesis 2.12, together with 3>48-49, and starts to gloss 'the name which the gods call love' as a reference to the Phaedrus, though the note is truncated at the page citation in the material consulted (farmer1998:23063).
historiography: Busi and Ebgi's apparatus identifies the two sources for 'the name by which the gods call love' as Plato, Phaedrus 252b, and Pseudo-Dionysius the Areopagite, De divinis nominibus I (589a) (busi2014:6542), and lists the thesis in their index of citations (busi2014:26620).
not_established: No further critical discussion of the thesis's argument, beyond identification of its two sources, is established by the sources consulted.
